summary: Implement Issue #5 scaffold/result isolation from the global-namespace kernel semantics (no namespace freezing): a private _restore_scaffold re-injects the official rlm_query bridge before every cell and in the outer finally so syntax/compile/query/runtime/repr/success exits all restore it; the fixed RESULT_NAME slot is deleted and a cell compiles into a statement body plus the final top-level expression as two code objects (both PyCF_ALLOW_TOP_LEVEL_AWAIT, positions preserved), capturing the expression value in an _on_eval local so no internal name is written, overwritten, popped or left in the user namespace; only CO_COROUTINE-flagged code objects are awaited (a bare awaitable last expression is returned as its repr, never auto-awaited); result formatting and truncation run inside the cell BaseException boundary before sys.stdout is restored and error frames use a raising-proof module-level _safe_str, so a raising __repr__/__str__ is a typed eval error and the same kernel/PID/globals keep serving. Existing error taxonomy, UTF-8 caps, persistent globals, top-level await, query bridge and Issue #1 lifecycle semantics are unchanged (src/runtime.ts untouched).

pointers: M1A Issue#5: a cell that shadows rlm_query cannot poison later cells
M1A Issue#5: deleting rlm_query in a failing cell is restored before the next cell
M1A Issue#5: an assignment-only cell after a result cell returns no stale result
M1A Issue#5: a user-defined __rlm_result__ is an ordinary persistent global
M1A Issue#5: a raising __repr__ is a typed eval error and the kernel survives
M1A Issue#5: a bare awaitable last expression is not auto-awaited
M1B Issue#5: a raising __repr__ is kind=eval and the same kernel keeps its globals

The framework (REPL probes, answer/context/history scaffolds, daemon) was not copied.

Confirmed the two-code-object semantics with a read-only Python 3.12.10 probe: compile(..., 'exec'|'eval', flags=ast.PyCF_ALLOW_TOP_LEVEL_AWAIT) sets CO_COROUTINE only for top-level-await code; eval of a coroutine-flagged code object returns a coroutine to await while a plain code object evaluates to its value/None; ast.Module/ast.Expression reconstruction with fix_missing_locations preserves positions and syntax-error reporting.

Added 6 M1A Issue#5 regressions (R1 shadow rlm_query, R2 delete-then-raise restore, R3 stale-result guard, R4 user __rlm_result__ persistence, R5 raising __repr__ typed error plus survival, bare-awaitable no-auto-await guard) and 1 M1B Issue#5 host-contract test (kind=eval and same PID/globals).

Ran the new tests on the untouched base: 5 FAIL / 42 PASS (R1 shadow returned error instead of query, R2 delete returned error instead of query, R4 user __rlm_result__ was popped to NameError, R5 M1A timed out because the kernel os._exit(1)'d on the raising repr, R5 M1B rejected kind=closed); R3 and the awaitable guard were already green on base, so both are recorded as regression guards rather than red gaps.

Implemented the minimal fix in python-runtime/rlm_kernel.py only: _restore_scaffold before every cell plus the outer finally; deleted RESULT_NAME and the _MISSING sentinel; split body and final-expression code objects; await only on CO_COROUTINE; format/truncate inside the BaseException boundary before sys.stdout restore; hardened _error_frame with module-level _safe_str.

Mid-candidate blocker identified by the coordinator in a parallel static check and fixed by me as implementer: the first form kept _safe_str as a @staticmethod but called self._safe_str from another static method, so every error path raised NameError and escalated to kernel os._exit(1); the implementer fixed it by making _safe_str module-level and confirmed through the error-path regressions (runtime/syntax/query/R2/R5) that typed errors no longer fatal the kernel.
